Nalanda University opens new sustainability school

Nalanda University on Saturday inaugurated its school of sustainability studies, which will admit its first batch of 120 students in the next academic session.

The school will offer programmes in ecology, water management and climate-resilient agriculture, drawing faculty from partner institutions in five countries.

Vice-chancellor officials said the curriculum blends ancient Indian knowledge systems with contemporary research methods.

Students welcomed the announcement, though some sought clarity on hostel capacity and scholarship coverage for the new batch.

The university, revived as an international institution a decade ago, now hosts over 500 students from 20 countries.
